sections.h2: What our lawn health service covers
paras: Every lawn care Canberra program starts with a look at the grass type, the soil, the shade and how the lawn is used. From there we build a plan that might include slow-release fertiliser in spring and autumn, a targeted spray for bindi and broadleaf weeds, and aeration advice if the soil has compacted.

Timing matters more than product. Feeding a frost-burnt lawn in June does very little, while the same feed in September lands as the spring growth surge begins. We schedule visits around that calendar, not a fixed date.

sections.h2: Canberra's climate and what it does to lawns
paras: Canberra grows cool-climate lawns. Kikuyu, couch, buffalo and tall fescue mixes are all common. Hard frosts from May to August turn kikuyu and couch brown while fescue holds its colour. Hot, dry summers then push the same lawns hard, especially on north-facing blocks in Chapman and Rivett.

The pressure points are predictable. Bindi and broadleaf weeds germinate in late winter and spring, so weed control is most effective from August before they set seed. Spring feeding from September supports the growth surge. Autumn feeding builds root reserves before frost. Good lawn care Canberra wide follows that rhythm, which is why we do not sell one visit in January and call it a program.

A lawn that looks worn out after winter is not always dead. Frost-burnt kikuyu and couch usually green up once the soil warms, so we often advise patience through August, then a feed once new growth shows. Bare patches from dog urine, shade or foot traffic need loosened soil, seed or runners, and water to establish.

Lawn care Canberra wide is mostly about thickening grass, because weedy lawns are usually a sign of thin turf rather than strong weeds. Our program treats the weeds and feeds the grass at the same time, so there is less bare soil for the next seeds to land in.

faqs.q: Is your lawn care Canberra wide or only Woden and Belconnen?
faqs.a: We run lawn health programs across Canberra. Weston Creek is our priority area, and we also cover Woden Valley, Belconnen, Tuggeranong, the Inner North and Inner South, and into Queanbeyan and Jerrabomberra. Call 0423 720 317 with your suburb.

faqs.q: My lawn went brown over winter in Pearce. Is it dead?
faqs.a: Probably not. Kikuyu and couch go dormant and brown under Canberra frosts from May to August, then recover once the soil warms in spring. If it is still brown by mid-October, or bare in patches, it is worth a look. We can assess it and quote a spring recovery plan.

faqs.q: When should I spray bindi in Canberra?
faqs.a: Late winter to early spring, from about August, before the plants flower and set their spiky seeds. Once you can feel the prickles it is too late for that season. Combine the spray with a spring feed so the grass fills the gaps, which is how most lawn care Canberra programs are built.

faqs.q: Can you do the mowing as well as the lawn care?
faqs.a: Yes. Lawn care Canberra programs can sit alongside a regular mowing schedule, with fertilising and weed control added at the right points in the year. One business, one quote, and green waste removal available with each mow.

faqs.q: Do I need to water after fertilising?
faqs.a: Yes. A good soak helps the fertiliser move into the soil and lowers the risk of burning the leaf. We plan applications around forecast rain where we can, and keep water restrictions in mind. Ask us about watering when you book.
